title: 1960 AHSME Problem 29
statement: Five times \(A\)’s money added to \(B\)’s money is more than \(\$51.00.\) Three times \(A\)’s money minus \(B\)’s money is \(\$21.00.\) If \(a\) represents \(A\)’s money in dollars and \(b\) represents \(B\)’s money in dollars, then:

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: \(a>9,\) but we can put no bounds on \(b\)

solutions.text:
From \(3a-b=21,\) we have \(b=3a-21.\) Substitution into the inequality gives \[ 5a+3a-21>51, \] so \(a>9.\) It follows that \(b=3a-21>6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use \(3a-b=21\) to express \(b\) in terms of \(a\)
